reviewScale.PASS: No blocking contradiction or unauthorized freeze; suitable to proceed to visual-reference evidence authoring.
reviewScale.REVISE: Useful structure but one or more blocking clarity/source/open-boundary issues must be corrected before visual evidence.
reviewScale.HOLD: Upstream authority is insufficient or contradictory; do not proceed with this board.

globalReviewDimensions.question: Does the board clearly distinguish Current/Research-backed content from OPEN or future candidates without turning research context into Story Canon?
Can the era difference be understood from ordinary systems, access, repair, transport, records, provisioning and friction rather than clothing or nostalgia alone?

If character faces and clothing were hidden, would this board still be distinguishable from the other four eras through communication, movement, shopping, repair, exchange, privacy, household access, task friction and material infrastructure?
Does the board avoid poverty cosplay, retro-catalog shorthand, smartphone-only present day, neon/chrome future shorthand, gender-role household shorthand and age caricatures?
Are exact year/place/product/household/family/technology details that remain unresolved still visibly OPEN?
Could a character artist, story artist, Lorebook implementer, stage artist or prop designer reuse the board without inventing missing era logic?
Do all five required panel roles carry distinct evidence rather than repeating the same mood or decorative information?

environmentSpecificReview: E01 shows multiple ordinary systems in use and is not cinematic key art.
E02 compares communication, transport/navigation, shopping/availability, repair/replacement and privacy/records.
E03 contains reusable ordinary prop/material evidence rather than decorative period props.
E04 shows at least two kinds of human use/friction without turning hardship into personality shorthand.
The board remains era-identifiable when costume, face and hero props are mentally removed.
populationHouseholdSpecificReview: P01 contains all six population lenses without implying literal family membership.
P02 shows at least three non-identical household/access situations.
P03 distributes at least four ordinary task categories without father/work mother/housework shorthand.
P04 compares at least three system-access axes.
P05 explicitly states that the board does not define the Core5 character's literal family/address/partner/children.
Population differences reinforce the era system without making one household structure representative of the era.
hardVetoes: board silently fixes an exact historical year that is OPEN
board silently fixes literal Core5 family members
board copies a real tragedy/incident into fictional Story authority
board presents a future research trajectory as proven future fact
board relies primarily on costume, sepia, neon, device stereotype or decorative signage to communicate era
board becomes indistinguishable from another Core5 era when faces, costume and hero props are ignored
board uses a generated candidate image as historical, family or Story authority
board removes OPEN/source labels for visual cleanliness
board claims Human approval, Master approval or runtime approval before explicit review
